summary: Session 94 merged premise-verified infrastructure audit with game-loop and public-release lenses. Session 93's five shipped items remain preserved. Five new findings survived live-code review: current-main CI is red on 1,588 bytes of Brotli entry overage; the globally mounted first-run tutorial opens over the lobby and consumes its seen state before the match surface exists; team Pressure can falsely complete personal First Extraction steps despite contributor evidence already being available; certified Daily Mastery accumulates into a number with no choice or non-power aspiration; and the startup brief presents completed audit work as a current hit list while PROJECT_STATUS embeds a large duplicate doctor transcript. External launch observations remain NO-GO and are not implementation claims.

infrastructure.result: Worker route reachability, browser-authored authority, remote-AI admission surfaces, lifecycle ownership, duplicated navigation producers, god-object boundaries, workflow freshness, dependency posture, and local release evidence were inspected against live sources.

gameLoop.result: The certified Capture-to-Breach loop and progression spine are strong. Live code nevertheless mounts first-contact instruction before the match, credits shared team Pressure as personal onboarding progress, and exposes Mastery as accumulation without an aspirational consumer. Retention remains unproven until real authenticated human sessions exist. Soul fidelity remains intentionally unscored because the public SOUL file contains no evaluable pillars.

release.toolingDisagreement: The portfolio release checker reports Private by default because context/STUDIO_MANIFEST.json intentionally says privateByDefault=false for this already-public, sanitized AGPL-derived repository. AGENTS.md explicitly declares the repository public. The mismatch is recorded as a checker-premise defect and is not repaired by falsifying the local manifest or editing Studio Ops.

rejectedPremises.evidence: VaultFrontStatusUpdate already carries server-derived per-player contributors, and activity updates identify the exact actor. Team success is useful context but cannot truthfully stand in for the learner's own capture, convoy, or decisive-delivery action.

rejectedPremises.evidence: No checked-in qualifying human cohort exists. Code can close choice and feedback seams, but only real authenticated sessions may establish return intent or fun.

items.title: Make live narration inherit server-certified match authority
items.why: NarratorReporter lets any browser POST an arbitrary activity and label for any gameId into NarratorBus. The server validates shape and IP rate only; it does not verify actor membership, live game ownership, or that the event occurred. GameServer imports NarratorBus only to close it, so AI commentary can be driven by browser-authored fiction.
items.recipe: Project a privacy-minimal narration event only after GameServer accepts authoritative intents and certified lifecycle outcomes; remove the public narrator event mutation and client reporter; preserve bounded SSE subscription; define a typed event catalog with no actor identifiers; lower the public-ingest ceiling; and prove fake game IDs, rejected intents, duplicate events, and browser posts cannot trigger commentary.

L2.recipe: Emit narration from accepted GameServer events and remove the client reporter.

L3.recipe: Certified typed projection, privacy-minimal deduplication, route-policy contraction, integrity counters, and adversarial tests.

executionLog: Removed the browser-writable narrator event route and NarratorReporter client mutation.
Added a typed privacy-minimal projection after GameServer intent admission; rejected intents and caller prose cannot enter narration.
Added a deterministic certified baseline with optional remote enrichment, a visible aria-live consumer, and adversarial authority tests.
Contract result: 29 declared/registered mutations, public ingest 4/4.

items.title: Give every runtime feature authority a reachable consumer or retire it
items.why: Worker exposes multiple feature surfaces with no client, agent, or operator consumer: match-mission, match-commentary, bot-lore, match-coach, clan-war, and parallel Intel market routes. The Intel routes accept caller identities, keep unbounded game maps, return random fallback risk, advertise a 2,000-gold cost, and never mutate the certified economy. Unused Api helpers also preserve phantom battle-narrative and bot-persona authority.
items.recipe: Create an executable runtime-feature reachability catalog that binds each admitted route to a source consumer and audience. Remove unreachable routes, imports, stores, client helpers, policies, and tests; keep core in-match Intel commands as the sole economy authority; forbid random quote data and uncharged cost claims; ratchet Worker and public-ingest ceilings downward; and mutation-test reintroduction.

L1.recipe: Remove the unconsumed Intel HTTP market and random quote fallback.

L2.recipe: Retire all verified unreachable feature clusters and reconcile policies/imports.

L3.recipe: Source-backed reachability catalog, measurable composition contraction, exact route-policy ceilings, and negative reintroduction tests.

executionLog: Retired fourteen verified unreachable routes across battle narrative, commentary, missions, bot lore/persona, match coach, Intel HTTP market, clan war, and browser narrator ingestion.
Removed the unreachable ClanWarStore and client helpers while preserving and explicitly cataloging the live micro-coach and progression router.
Added a source-backed catalog for eight admitted route→transport→consumer chains, fourteen retired-route tombstones, mutation tests, doctor coverage, and a sha256 evidence digest.
Worker contracted from 2,849 audited lines to 2,420 with a 2,440-line ratchet.

items.title: Make pre-match intelligence bounded, abortable, and stale-session-proof
items.why: GameStartingModal launches three provider-backed requests with Promise.all and owns neither an AbortController nor a session generation. hide() leaves requests and two timeouts alive; an earlier match can overwrite a later modal, and the fixed 300px surface can overflow when all three cards arrive on mobile. There is no focused lifecycle test.
items.recipe: Introduce a generation-scoped pre-match session with AbortController, bounded per-task deadlines, all-settled status, timer cleanup, stale-result rejection, and exact hide/disconnect teardown. Render an accessible responsive shell with deterministic loading/degraded states, validate provider payloads before projection, and capture desktop/mobile evidence across all themes.

L1.recipe: Reject stale async results and clear timers on hide.

L2.recipe: Add abort signals, per-task deadlines, and lifecycle tests.

L3.recipe: Session receipt, accessible responsive state machine, three-theme desktop/mobile rendered proof, and exact cleanup invariants.

executionLog: Added generation ownership, AbortController propagation, a six-second deadline, all-settled projection, stale-result rejection, and exact timer teardown.
Added accessible loading/degraded/ready states and a 92vw/32rem, 85dvh responsive dialog.
Focused lifecycle tests prove hide abort and cross-match stale suppression; the three-state desktop/mobile/theme matrix is included in the 90-artifact visual receipt.

items.title: Generate static and in-app public navigation from one route graph
items.why: public/footer-manifest.json generates and validates ten static pages, but the Lit application footer repeats routes, copyright, brand, and attribution by hand. It omits the required Play destination and adds Wiki/Source links outside the checked graph, so the green footer gate does not cover the actual app footer.
items.recipe: Make one typed public route manifest drive static shell generation and the Lit footer projection, explicitly classify app-only external links, and extend the scoped checker to validate the application consumer. Preserve ordering, labels, legal pages, branding, upstream attribution, and current visual output; add digest/reachability tests and close the local half of the aged SIL item without claiming staging screenshots.

L1.recipe: Import footer links from the existing manifest into the app.

L2.recipe: Type the manifest and include app-only external links.

L3.recipe: One projection authority, app/static parity checker, digest evidence, and drift mutation tests.

executionLog: Created src/shared/PublicRouteGraph.json as the canonical typed route graph and kept public/footer-manifest.json as an exact checked mirror.
The static shell generator and Lit footer now project the same seven routes, ownership, copyright, attribution, and two classified app-external links.
Footer checker now validates app consumption, mirror parity, hard-coded-route absence, and a sha256 graph digest.

items.title: Turn transport recovery evidence into calm player-visible state
items.why: Transport now emits exact connection state, retry attempt, outbox depth, and overflow events, but only tests consume them. Players see no waiting/recovering/synchronized feedback, queued actions are invisible, and protocol refusal still uses blocking alert(), bypassing the app's accessible modal and theme system.
items.recipe: Add a dedicated recovery presenter subscribed to transport state/overflow events: a non-blocking aria-live banner for waiting/recovering/synchronized states, queued-action count and reject-newest overflow guidance, and an accessible fatal-refusal modal. Keep transient states generation-safe, never claim synchronized before rejoin succeeds, test event-to-view semantics, and capture all themes at desktop/mobile widths.

L1.recipe: Replace alert() with the existing modal path.

L2.recipe: Render waiting/recovery/overflow state from transport events.

L3.recipe: Accessible generation-safe presenter, honest synchronization lifecycle, theme/mobile proof, and adversarial event tests.

executionLog: Added an accessible player-visible presenter for connecting, waiting, synchronizing, restored, fatal refusal, and reject-newest overflow states.
Removed blocking alert(), sanitized fatal reason text, and bound retry/outbox language to exact transport events.
Reordered transport truth so open is published only after authoritative rejoin and FIFO flush; focused tests prove one zero-depth open event.
All five states pass desktop/mobile/theme rendered proof.

items.title: Make first contact begin inside the match fantasy and recover transfer headroom
items.why: Main.ts statically imports and mounts VaultFrontTutorial during lobby bootstrap. Its 800ms timer opens instructions for an in-match tracker that does not exist yet, and dismissing it permanently consumes the versioned seen state. The lobby hero simultaneously exposes internal visual-pass/changelog language. The same eager surface contributes to a current-main CI failure: initial Brotli entry is 594,207 bytes against a 592,619-byte ceiling.
items.recipe: Replace timer-driven lobby mounting with one match-ready signal emitted only after authoritative VaultFront status reaches the mounted ControlPanel. Lazy-load the tutorial behind that signal, preserve exactly-once shown/skip/complete telemetry, cancel listeners and timers on teardown, and rewrite the lobby hero around the Capture → Convoy → Pressure → Breach fantasy. Prove no lobby display/seen mutation, one match display, teardown safety, and a directly green unchanged bundle ceiling; capture the touched lobby and in-match states across every theme at desktop/mobile widths.

L1.recipe: Remove the lobby auto-open timer and internal-process hero copy.

L2.recipe: Gate a lazy tutorial on a match-ready event and add lifecycle tests.

L3.recipe: Authoritative match-bound state machine, exactly-once telemetry, lazy chunk/transfer proof, adversarial lifecycle tests, and full rendered-pixel matrix.

executionLog: Removed timer-driven lobby presentation; first contact now lazy-loads only after ControlPanel receives the first authoritative VaultFront status.
Rewrote the lobby hero around Capture → Convoy → Pressure → Breach and preserved exactly-once shown/advance/skip/complete telemetry.
Split tutorial, lobby, and leaderboard secondary UI from the initial entry; unchanged Brotli gate is green at 588,569 bytes against 592,619 bytes.
Focused tutorial, authority, HUD, TypeScript, and bundle contracts pass.

items.title: Give First Extraction a server-derived personal agency ledger
items.why: Vault Pressure is player-or-team scoped and already projects contributors by actor, but ControlPanel passes the shared pressure state into advanceFirstExtractionProgress. That projector promotes pressureStarted into vaultCaptured and convoyAction and promotes team victory into decisiveDelivery, so a teammate can complete the learner's personal capture, convoy, and winning-delivery steps.
items.recipe: Separate team context from personal evidence. Recover personal capture from actor activity or controlled-site state, convoy engagement from actor activity or the contributor ledger, personal Pressure from contributors, and decisive delivery only from the exact vault_breach_victory actor. Let team threshold/window state advance only the explicitly team-labeled step after personal participation. Preserve reconnect recovery from status, forbid retroactive teammate credit, expose a compact personal/team evidence receipt for the tracker, and add solo/team/reconnect/adversarial tests plus rendered states.

L1.recipe: Stop later team Pressure from implying personal capture and convoy action.

L2.recipe: Consume contributors and exact actor activity for personal step ownership.

L3.recipe: Reconnect-safe personal/team ledger, explicit copy, receipt semantics, adversarial team tests, and rendered proof.

executionLog: Removed every team-state implication into personal capture, convoy, Pressure contribution, and completion evidence.
Personal capture recovers from exact actor activity or controlled-site status; convoy and Pressure recover from exact actor activity and the server-derived contributor ledger.
Team threshold/window advances only the explicitly team-labelled Breach step after personal contribution; decisive delivery requires the exact vault_breach_victory actor.
Completion now requires all five personally truthful steps, with adversarial shared-Pressure tests.

items.title: Turn certified Mastery into a player-chosen non-power Doctrine Vault
items.why: Certified Daily Mastery awards durable currency and the live sidebar displays only '<balance> M total'. There is no catalog, entitlement threshold, selection, spend path, or downstream consumer, so the retention hook accumulates obligation without aspiration. The wallet already has transactional PostgreSQL and process-local parity, making a bounded non-power choice layer feasible without retuning gameplay.
items.recipe: Add a versioned Doctrine catalog of cosmetic/coaching identities with no combat-stat effects. Implement an authenticated, rate-limited, replay-safe select-or-unlock transaction that atomically deducts Mastery once, persists entitlements and the active Doctrine in PostgreSQL with process-local parity, and returns an explicit receipt. Surface next unlock, owned choices, active Doctrine, durability, and insufficient-funds truth in the sidebar; use the selected Doctrine only to frame existing coaching/next-match goals. Add route-policy coverage, migration, concurrent/idempotent store tests, client schema validation, and desktop/mobile/theme rendered proof.

L1.recipe: Expose a static non-power unlock catalog and next threshold.

L2.recipe: Add authenticated replay-safe unlock/select with durable entitlement state.

L3.recipe: Transactional PostgreSQL/process-local parity, route-policy admission, active coaching identity, concurrency tests, receipts, and rendered choice states.

executionLog: Added a server-owned three-Doctrine catalog explicitly limited to coaching and identity, never combat power.
Added authenticated, rate-limited, schema-validated, replay-safe select-or-unlock with atomic wallet deduction and PostgreSQL/process-local parity.
Added durable unlock, active-profile, and request-receipt tables plus owned/active/affordability UI and honest insufficient-funds receipts.
Focused store, router, policy, UI, TypeScript, and 30/30 mutation-route coverage contracts pass.

items.title: Make the startup hit list distinguish actionable work from shipped history
items.why: generate-genius-list maps shipped audit items to done, but renderBrief prints the first entries regardless of status. The S94 startup brief therefore announces Unblocked 0 while presenting five checked completed items under GENIUS HIT LIST, and /start surfaces a completed item as the top action.
items.recipe: Render only actionable entries in the hit list. When none exist, emit a source-derived exhaustion tile with shipped/pending/blocked totals, latest audit identity, and the next expansion command; keep full completed history in GENIUS_LIST.md/cache. Add tests for mixed, exhausted, blocked-only, and malformed sidecars, then re-render and validate the canonical brief.

L1.recipe: Filter done items from the brief.

L2.recipe: Add explicit exhausted and blocked-only states with counts.

L3.recipe: Source-derived taxonomy ledger, adversarial sidecar tests, cache/Markdown parity, and canonical brief validation.

executionLog: Extracted one fail-closed genius-brief taxonomy authority and removed completed history from the actionable hit list.
Added source-derived exhausted and blocked-only tiles with contiguous actionable ranks and an innovation-pack continuation command.
Mixed, exhausted, blocked-only, malformed, and generator contract tests pass.

items.title: Separate compact project health from full doctor evidence
items.why: PROJECT_STATUS.json embeds all thirteen doctor checks including duplicated child-process commands, stdout payloads, timestamps, and parsed data. Every startup/status consumer pays for the full transcript even though normal rendering uses only aggregate counts; warning ownership is the only path that needs check detail.
items.recipe: Write the complete doctor report to one atomic hash-bound audits/doctor-latest.json sidecar and keep only aggregate counts, observation time, source, evidence path, and SHA-256 digest in PROJECT_STATUS. Teach startup warning classification to load and verify the sidecar only when warnings/failures exist, fail closed on missing or mismatched detail, and retain backwards-compatible reads for legacy embedded checks. Add tamper/missing/legacy/green-path tests and measure the status-token reduction.

L1.recipe: Move doctor checks into a dedicated sidecar.

L2.recipe: Bind the compact summary to the sidecar digest and lazy-load non-green detail.

L3.recipe: Atomic write, fail-closed verification, legacy migration, tamper tests, and measured token/byte delta.

executionLog: Moved full doctor checks into an atomic audits/doctor-latest.json evidence sidecar bound to compact project status by SHA-256.
Startup now lazy-loads detail only for non-green health, fails closed on missing/tampered evidence, and retains legacy embedded-check compatibility.
Atomic reload, tamper, unsafe-path, missing, legacy, project-doctor, and startup contracts pass.
